BEHIND THE IMAGE

A map of geometry.
A window into time.

We model the exterior of a non-rotating, spherical mass using the Schwarzschild metric. Everything is measured in Schwarzschild radii (rₛ) and light-crossing times (rₛ/c).

Space view
The surface is Flamm’s paraboloid: an isometric embedding of an equatorial, constant-time spatial slice. Its vertical depth represents spatial curvature. It is not a physical funnel or the time dimension.
The clocks
These clocks are held at fixed radii, requiring support. Their proper time follows dτ/dt = √(1 − rₛ/r), relative to the coordinate time of a distant stationary observer. Markers are enlarged for visibility.
The light
Traces are numerically integrated null geodesics of the Schwarzschild spacetime, projected onto this spatial slice. They do not follow paths calculated from the drawn surface alone. Traces stop just outside the horizon; crossing is not shown in finite Schwarzschild coordinate time.
Time view
Two spatial coordinates are retained and coordinate time is drawn vertically. The horizontal plane is your selected “now”; marks on each clock’s worldline show equal increments of its own proper time. Spatial curvature is not embedded in this view. The transition between views is a visual morph.
